name: Dravite
physical: Traditionally associated with steadiness and stamina
Said to bring a settled feeling to the body
Crystal healers link it with comfort in the digestive area
summary: Dravite is the earthy brown magnesium tourmaline, a grounding stone in crystal lore for stability, patience and a solid, trusting connection to home.
intro: Dravite is the brown member of the tourmaline family, found in shades from honey and chestnut to dark chocolate. It is rich in magnesium rather than iron, which gives it its warm tones and sometimes a golden glint. Crystals form stout, striated prisms with a rounded triangular cross-section, and large specimens often sit in white marble or schist, making a handsome display. Because the colour is so earthy, many collectors see it as the quiet cousin of black tourmaline: not a stone of drama, but of steady, reliable presence. Gem-quality dravite, sometimes called brown tourmaline, can also be faceted into rich, tea-coloured jewels.
history: Dravite takes its name from the Drava River region in Carinthia, Austria and Slovenia, where it was first described in the nineteenth century by the Austrian mineralogist Gustav Tschermak. The Drava region, with its alpine valleys, gave the mineral its identity as a distinct tourmaline species. Fine specimens later came from Kenya, Tanzania and Sri Lanka, where yellowish-brown stones also appear. In Tanzania a particularly attractive golden-brown variety became known as chocolate tourmaline. Because it is common and durable, dravite has never been a luxury gem, but lapidaries enjoy it for its warm colour and fine polish.
meaning: Dravite is considered a stone of home, roots and practical reassurance. Crystal practitioners say it helps people feel steady when circumstances shift, and it is often suggested for anyone who is moving house, starting a new job or simply needs a gentler pace. Its colour ties it to the root chakra and to the element of earth, and it is said to calm anxious thoughts about money or security. Unlike flashier stones, dravite is often kept as a quiet companion rather than a talisman for dramatic change. Healers also link it with patience in family life and with cultivating small daily routines. Physically it is traditionally associated with stamina and a settled stomach, though it is a comfort stone only and never a replacement for medical advice.
howToUse: Carry a tumbled dravite in a pocket on days when you feel scattered. During meditation sit with a piece in each hand and picture roots growing from the soles of your feet into the earth. Place a stone near the front door or in a living room to encourage a settled, welcoming atmosphere. Keep one in your desk drawer to support steady work habits, or set it beside the bed if you worry about tomorrow. Pair it with black tourmaline for grounding and protection, or with citrine for practical abundance.
care: Dravite is hard and water-safe, so a gentle rinse in lukewarm water is enough for cleansing, followed by a soft dry cloth. It also responds well to smoke, sound or a bed of sea salt in a dry container. Sunlight is generally fine, and brief sun charging is a good option. Avoid hard knocks, which can chip the tips of raw prisms, and wrap crystals separately in cloth so they do not scratch softer minerals nearby.
identify: Genuine dravite shows lengthwise striations on raw crystals, a glassy shine and a brown to yellow-brown colour that may shift slightly with the viewing angle. Common look-alikes include smoky quartz, brown garnet, axinite, brown zircon and glass. Tourmaline is pyroelectric and piezoelectric, so a warmed crystal may attract light dust or paper scraps. Most dravite is untreated, although occasional stones may be heated. Compare with schorl, which is black, and uvite, a similar calcium-rich brown tourmaline that can be hard to distinguish without testing.

faq.a: Crystal practitioners use dravite for grounding, patience and a feeling of home. It is often chosen during transitions to promote a steady, practical outlook and a quiet sense of safety.

faq.q: Is dravite the same as brown tourmaline?
faq.a: Mostly. Dravite is the magnesium-rich brown species of tourmaline, while uvite is a similar calcium-rich brown one. Both are commonly sold as brown tourmaline, and the difference matters mainly to mineralogists.

faq.q: Can dravite be used in water?
faq.a: Yes. With a hardness around 7 to 7.5 and no soluble components, dravite is safe for rinsing and for indirect-method gem water. Avoid thermal shocks, such as moving it from hot to icy water.
